name: work-cycle
summary: A development cycle for every repository on one machine: a first run that writes the backlog as task records, a foreground task runner that serves registered repositories through one first-in, first-out queue during working hours, delivery that pushes a task branch and opens a labelled pull or merge request that a person merges, and edit and pre-push guards.
runtime: Python 3.11 or later and Git, on Windows, WSL2, macOS or Linux; gh, glab or az for opening requests, each optional
inputs: Task records and handoffs in the folders project.json names
The cycle object and the checks in project.json
runner.json in the runner's home folder
evidence: A run record per task run in the runner's home folder
A delivery record per delivery in the repository's Git folder
tested: none: the tests run every command against disposable repositories with stand-in review tools and agents on Linux, Windows and macOS; no real host, agent client or work repository has used it.
manual: Keep task records by hand, start agent sessions yourself in a new worktree, push task branches and open requests in the host's web page, and protect the default branch in the host's settings.
